Dam Site
A marker left by an older version of Dams. Yields as the land beneath it, and is lifted when the game loads.

Adds a Dam building to each age, unlocked by Irrigation, Machinery and Electricity. Build it on any river tile, navigable or not. It yields Food and Production, and once it is finished, floods stop pillaging the improvements, buildings and districts of its settlement: an Ancient Dam holds back moderate floods, a Medieval Dam major ones as well, and a Modern Dam every flood. In single player the other settlements on the dammed river share that protection through a Levee, and the river's floodplains dry out behind the Dam, giving up their Food for good. Each Dam a settlement already has makes the next one there cost more.

Dams
Basics

A Dam is a building placed on a river tile: a Navigable River, or a land tile with a Minor River. It yields [icon:YIELD_FOOD] Food and [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION] Production wherever it stands, and once it is finished, floods no longer pillage the Improvements, Buildings and Districts of its [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_SETTLEMENT_TOOLTIP]Settlement[/TIP].

Each age has its own Dam, and each holds back larger floods than the one before. A Dam pays its yields on any river, so it is worth building on a river that never floods; on one that does, it also guards the Settlement.
Dams by Age

[BLIST][LI][B]Ancient Dam[/B] (Antiquity): unlocked by Irrigation. Costs 150 [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION] Production and 1 [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold a turn. +2 [icon:YIELD_FOOD] Food, +2 [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION] Production. Holds back moderate floods.[LI][B]Medieval Dam[/B] (Exploration): unlocked by Machinery. Costs 275 [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION] Production and 2 [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold a turn. +3 [icon:YIELD_FOOD] Food, +3 [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION] Production. Holds back moderate and major floods.[LI][B]Modern Dam[/B] (Modern): unlocked by Electricity. Costs 600 [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION] Production and 3 [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold a turn. +4 [icon:YIELD_FOOD] Food, +6 [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION] Production. Holds back every flood, the 1000-year flood included.[/LIST]
Placement

A Dam is built from the production list or bought with [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold, in a City or a Town, on any river tile where the Settlement could place a building. A young Settlement is offered only the river tiles beside its City Center, and more as it grows.

Any river can take a Dam, and a Settlement on two rivers can dam both. What holds the number down is the price: each Dam of an age a Settlement already has adds about a quarter of the base cost to the next one there (+40, +70 and +150 [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION] Production for the Ancient, Medieval and Modern Dam), and every Dam pays its [icon:YIELD_GOLD] Gold upkeep.
Other Civilizations

Computer-controlled players build Dams by the same rules and at the same price, and weigh them as they weigh any other building. Single player and multiplayer games use the same rules too, except for Levees and dried Floodplains (see Levees).
Flood Protection
Flood Sizes

Floods come in three sizes: moderate, major and 1000-year. A flood a Dam holds back does not pillage Improvements, Buildings or Districts in a protected Settlement. A larger flood than the Dam can hold does damage as usual.

A Dam does not stop the flood itself. Floods on a dammed river still happen, are still reported, and still leave silt behind, raising the [icon:YIELD_FOOD] Food or [icon:YIELD_PRODUCTION] Production of one to three of the river's tiles.
Who Is Protected
The Settlement holding the Dam, always. In single player also every other Settlement that owns a tile of the dammed river, including those of other players, through a Levee.
Protection belongs to the whole Settlement, not to one river. A Settlement on the dammed river and on a second river is protected on both.
Damage Prevented

Larger floods are rarer and pillage more of the tiles they reach (20%, 40% and 60% of flooded tiles). Weighed by both, the share of flood damage each Dam prevents at each Disaster Frequency, Light (the default), Moderate and Catastrophic, is:[BLIST][LI][B]Ancient Dam:[/B] about 17%, 29%, 36%.[LI][B]Medieval Dam:[/B] about 50%, 57%, 73%.[LI][B]Modern Dam:[/B] all of it.[/LIST]
Overtopped Dams

A flood bigger than a Dam can hold pillages the Dam itself if it reaches the Dam's tile: a major or 1000-year flood an Ancient Dam, a 1000-year flood a Medieval Dam. The Modern Dam holds every flood and is never overtopped. A pillaged Dam gives no yields and no protection until it is repaired, and in single player the Levees along its river fall back to the next best Dam.
Dried Floodplains

In single player and hotseat games, when a Dam is finished every [TIP:LOC_PEDIA_CONCEPTS_FLOODPLAINS_TOOLTIP]Floodplain[/TIP] on its river is removed, along the whole river and whoever owns the tile. Each of those tiles loses the Floodplain's own yield, about 1 [icon:YIELD_FOOD] Food, for good, and the Floodplains do not return if the Dam is razed. A river with no Floodplains costs nothing.
Drying does not stop the floods: they come as before and still leave their silt.
Levees
Basics

A Levee carries a Dam's protection to the other Settlements on its river. It is placed in the City Center of every Settlement that owns a tile of a dammed river, and holds back the same floods as the best finished Dam on that river.

A Levee cannot be built or bought. It takes no building slot and needs no citizen. A Settlement already holding a Dam at least as good as the river's best has no Levee. A Settlement on two dammed rivers gets the Levee of the better Dam.
When Levees Change

[BLIST][LI]A Settlement founded on a dammed river, or whose borders grow to reach one, gets its Levee at the start of the next turn.[LI]When a newer Dam is finished on the river, its Levees are raised to match.[LI]When a Dam is pillaged or razed, the Levees along its river fall back to the next best Dam, or are removed if there is none, a turn later.[LI]A Settlement that loses its last tile of the river loses its Levee a turn later.[/LIST]
Multiplayer

Levees are placed, and Floodplains dried, in single player and hotseat games only. In an online or LAN game each Dam protects the Settlement that holds it and the river keeps its Floodplains; everything else about Dams is the same.
